verified_by: 3-state differential (Maven, JDK 17) on the real production EventProcessingConfig.xStream() bean
note: Second native-Maven Axon/CQRS external production case (after xstream-axon-artshishkin). Same xstream 1.4.18 default-deny mechanism, independent repo/domain type. Repo targets Java 17 / Axon 4.9.3.
discovery_method: One of the 12 verifiable production candidates in output/xstream-1.4.17-to-1.4.19-forbiddenclass_candidates.jsonl (repo amirsnw/chainrtrade-axon-CQRS-DDD, sha d408d4ca).

library.dependency_scope: compile (transitive via org.axonframework axon-spring-boot-starter 4.9.3; resolves xstream 1.4.20 by default)

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: born past the boundary (transitive via Axon, pinned once)
in_repo_version_transition.evidence: axon-spring-boot-starter 4.9.3 was pinned in the initial commit 42dd97c (2025) and never bumped; it pulls xstream 1.4.20 from the repo's birth. The project never crossed 1.4.18 in its own history — it adopted the allowlist for a break that was LATENT in the version it started on (adaptation-to-the-break, not to a witnessed transition).

bump_provenance.summary: There is NO commit in this repo that bumps xstream. The boundary-crossing xstream version was never chosen or upgraded by the developer — it arrived transitively through the Axon starter, which was pinned once at project creation.
bump_provenance.how_introduced_transitively: The app never declares com.thoughtworks.xstream:xstream directly. It depends on org.axonframework:axon-spring-boot-starter 4.9.3, and Axon uses XStream as its default event/command serializer, so the starter pulls xstream in transitively. Maven resolves that transitive dependency to xstream 1.4.20 (already past the 1.4.18 default-deny boundary). So from the very first build the app runs on a post-1.4.18 xstream without any explicit version being written anywhere.
evidence: `git log -S 'xstream' -- '**/pom.xml'` over the full history returns NOTHING — the xstream version string never appears in any committed pom.

No pom declares a com.thoughtworks.xstream dependency (the only such line, product-service/pom.xml, is the explicit dep ADDED by the verification harness to pin the version for the differential — not an app commit).
axon.version (4.9.3) is set once, in the initial commit 42dd97c, and is never bumped afterward — so the transitive xstream version is fixed from project creation.
`mvn dependency:tree -Dverbose` shows `com.thoughtworks.xstream:xstream:jar:1.4.20:compile` reached only through the Axon dependency chain.
bump_provenance.why_it_still_breaks: Because the resolved xstream (1.4.20) is already on the default-deny side of the 1.4.18 boundary, the break is present at runtime the moment the app serializes its own domain type through Axon's XStream — no upgrade event is needed to trigger it. The developer discovered it as a runtime ForbiddenClassException and responded with the adaptation commit (see `adaptation.commit`), which is the only xstream-related commit in the repo.
bump_provenance.consequence_for_the_dataset: The 'library version transition' is implicit in the dependency tree rather than materialized as a diff. The 3-state differential recreates the transition synthetically (pinning xstream 1.4.17 -> 1.4.19 via the harness dep) to isolate the version + the adaptation as the only variables.

adaptation.repo_note: A ChainTrade Axon/CQRS-DDD project (Spring Boot + Axon 4.9.3, Java 17). Multi-module Maven; 'core' holds the shared domain types, 'product-service' holds the XStream @Bean config.
adaptation.commit_message: fix: resolve XStream ForbiddenClassException for ProductRestModel package migration
adaptation.confound_note: The fix commit also migrates ProductRestModel to the com.chaintrade.core.model package. The differential is unaffected: it contrasts a plain new XStream() against the production EventProcessingConfig.xStream(), at the adapted commit, swapping ONLY the xstream version, so the package move is held constant across all three states.
adaptation.in_repo_causal_evidence: Commit message names the exact exception (ForbiddenClassException) and the fix (XStream security configuration allowing the domain packages).
adaptation.summary: Added a production @Bean XStream that allowlists the app's domain packages on the XStream Axon uses, satisfying xstream 1.4.18 default-deny.

behavioral_break.mechanism: xstream 1.4.18+ default-deny: fromXML on a non-allowlisted class throws com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException. Axon uses XStream as its default serializer, so a plain XStream (no allowlist) rejects the app's own domain types under >=1.4.18.

verification.method: 3-state differential at the adapted commit (Maven, JDK 17). EventProcessingConfig.xStream() is a plain callable method, so the differential contrasts plain `new XStream()` (faithful stand-in for Axon's pre-adaptation default) against the production `new EventProcessingConfig().xStream()`, swapping only the xstream version.
verification.test: bbc.XstreamBbcTest (authored JUnit5; round-trip a ProductRestModel through XStream, assert productId survives). Preserved in scratchpad/xstream-chaintrade-amirsnw-harness/.
verification.harness_notes: product-service/pom.xml edited to add an EXPLICIT depth-1 xstream dependency version=${bbc.xstream.version} so the baseline override applies (otherwise xstream is pinned to 1.4.20 transitively by Axon). product-service already runs on the JUnit 5 platform, so no vintage engine needed.
verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC with a real external native-Maven production adaptation: baseline passes, the same plain-XStream code breaks only under xstream >=1.4.18 with a ForbiddenClassException on the app's own domain type, and the production EventProcessingConfig allowlist resolves it.
